# WooCommerce REST API

The WooCommerce REST API connects your store to external systems and services. Most integrations require you to generate API keys in WooCommerce and enter them in the external service to establish the connection. This document covers how to generate and manage REST API keys from a merchant perspective, with links to developer documentation for more advanced topics.

**Note:** You can find the [technical documentation](woocommerce.github.io/woocommerce-rest-api-docs/) for the REST API on GitHub.

...

To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user:

1. Go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API** .
2. Select **Create an API key** or **Add Key** . The **Key Details** screen opens.
3. Enter a **Description** to identify what the key is used for.
4. Select the **User** you want to generate a key for from the dropdown.
5. Select a level of access for this API key from the **Permissions** dropdown:
   
    + **Read** — allows the application to retrieve data from your store
    + **Write** — allows the application to create and update data in your store
    + **Read/Write** — allows the application both read and write access
6. Select **Generate API Key** .

After generating the key, the screen displays your **Consumer Key** , **Consumer Secret** , a **QR Code** , and a **Revoke Key** link. Copy the **Consumer Key** and **Consumer Secret** and enter them in the application you are connecting to. The application may also request your site URL.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) / Documentation

MCP for WooCommerce

MCP for WooCommerce by w7s connects Claude , ChatGPT , and other AI assistants to your WooCommerce store so they can work with your orders, products, customers, and more in plain language. It runs its own Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on the free MCP Adapter plugin, gives you a settings screen to manage the connection and your API keys, and lets you choose exactly which groups of tools the AI client is allowed to use. This guide covers what you need, how to set it up, what every setting does, and how developers can extend it.

Overview

↑ Back to top
MCP for WooCommerce gives your store its own MCP server. MCP is the standard that lets an AI assistant call tools on your site. The plugin’s server lives at /wp-json/w7s-mcp/v1/mcp and runs on the MCP Adapter, a free plugin from WordPress.org that handles the MCP protocol for WordPress.
It does three main things:
* It provides a settings area under WooCommerce > Settings > MCP for connecting an assistant, creating API keys, and reviewing activity;
* It registers a large set of MCP abilities so an assistant can list and manage orders, products, customers, coupons, refunds, tax, shipping, webhooks, reports, and more; and
* It lets you switch whole groups of tools (called tool packs) on or off, so an assistant only ever sees the capabilities you have chosen to expose.
On top of the server, the plugin adds the connection and key management screens, a large library of abilities, tool pack gating that is enforced when a tool runs, optional activity logging and change history, and API key permission enforcement on every call. It does not depend on WooCommerce’s own MCP feature, which WooCommerce removes in version 11.3.

...

Configurations made before 2.0.0 use /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp , which keeps working.
The API key authenticates each request. It is a WooCommerce REST API key in the form consumer_key:consumer_secret , sent in the X-MCP-API-Key header. The key’s permission scope is enforced on every call, so a read key cannot write no matter how a request is phrased. The user attached to the key also needs the manage_woocommerce capability.
From there, clients connect in one of three shapes:
* A local bridge. Claude Desktop runs a small helper on your machine that speaks to your store and presents the tools to the app. With the one-click bundle, the bridge ships inside the bundle; with the manual setup, it is the @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote package. The bridge reads the key from its local configuration and sends it as a header. Creating a connector URL also stores an encrypted replayable copy on the site, even if you ultimately use the Desktop bridge; see Manage API Keys .

...

↑ Back to top
No. From 2.0.0, MCP for WooCommerce runs its own MCP server and does not need WooCommerce’s MCP feature. It no longer switches that feature on, and leaves an existing setting unchanged.

WooCommerce’s notice says to use an Application Password. Should I?

↑ Back to top
No. That advice is for stores that used WooCommerce’s own MCP endpoint. MCP for WooCommerce keeps using WooCommerce REST API keys, which can be read-only and can be revoked one person at a time. See Why API keys and not Application Passwords .

Where do API keys come from?

↑ Back to top
They are standard WooCommerce REST API keys (a consumer key and secret). The plugin uses the key’s existing permission, so a read key cannot make changes. Create keys from the Connection tab, and manage them on the Advanced tab.

results.title: WooCommerce 11.3 MCP Adaptor updates Advisories – The WooCommerce Developer Blog
excerpts:
WooCommerce 11.3 MCP Adaptor updates

Darren Ethier Avatar
Darren Ethier
•
Oct 21, 2026
Advisories , Engineering
Starting with WooCommerce 11.3, WooCommerce core product and order abilities will be enabled by default, and will require the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin active on your store to establish an MCP connection.
This update will remove the /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint and legacy abilities that have been deprecated since WooCommerce 10.9 .
If your MCP client connects to your store with the deprecated endpoint and a WooCommerce REST API key, you will need to update that connection to use the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin and a WordPress application password before testing or upgrading to 11.3.

Enabling MCP in WooCommerce 11.3

MCP Adapter 0.7.0 is the first release published as a WordPress.org plugin, and it deprecates bundling the adapter as a Composer library . With one shared adapter per site, a separate WooCommerce endpoint with its own authentication and its own set of REST-shaped tools only added configuration and confusion.
The purpose-built WooCommerce abilities replace the REST-derived ones, and the adapter’s default server already exposes them, along with abilities registered by other plugins on your site. We’re also working on bringing more abilities to Woo core and our extensions to round out the type of actions and tools available for humans and agents working with WooCommerce.

What’s removed 

* The /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint and its WooCommerce REST API key authentication (the X-MCP-API-Key header). Requests to it now return HTTP 410 with a JSON-RPC error that explains how to connect through the MCP Adapter.
* The WooCommerce MCP feature ( mcp_integration ) under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features . FeaturesUtil::feature_is_enabled( 'mcp_integration' ) now always returns false .

...

If you connected an AI assistant to /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp :
1. Install and activate the MCP Adapter plugin , for example with wp plugin install mcp-adapter --activate .
2. Create a WordPress application password for a user with only the capabilities the client needs.
3. Point your MCP client at /wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server with that username and application password, instead of the WooCommerce endpoint and REST API key.
The WooCommerce MCP documentation has client configuration examples. Stores that had the WooCommerce MCP feature enabled see an admin notice after updating. It links to the documentation and, when no MCP adapter is loaded, to Install MCP Adapter (which opens the official plugin’s details) or Activate MCP Adapter if the plugin is already installed. The notice goes away for every admin once someone dismisses it or activates the plugin from it. You can revoke the WooCommerce REST API keys you created for the old endpoint.

excerpts:
* Product Feed Manager
WooCommerce AI / Documentation / WooCommerce AI / Connect an AI client to the WooCommerce AI MCP server

Connect an AI client to the WooCommerce AI MCP server

Connect an external Model Context Protocol (MCP) client to your store’s WooCommerce AI server. Use the endpoint generated for your store, then authorize the client and confirm a read-only request before allowing store changes.
Note :
This is a Developer level doc. If you are unfamiliar working with code and resolving potential conflicts, we recommend you work with a Woo Agency Partner for larger projects, or find a WooCommerce developer on Codeable for smaller customizations. We are unable to provide support for customizations under our Support Policy .

Prerequisites

↑ Back to top
* WooCommerce and WooCommerce AI are active.
* Your store and user account are connected to WordPress.com.
* Your account can manage WooCommerce.
* The MCP client supports remote HTTP servers and the authentication flow used by the endpoint.

Copy the store endpoint

↑ Back to top
1. In WordPress admin, go to WooCommerce > Settings > WooCommerce AI > Advanced > MCP server .
2. Enable Progressive MCP server if it is off.
3. Open Setup , choose your client, and copy the generated server URL or configuration.
The WordPress.com URL includes your store identifier. Its structure is:
public-api.wordpress.com/wpcom/v2/sites/{site}/woocommerce-ai-mcp/v1
Copy the complete URL from your store’s Setup screen, including its store identifier.

Example: Claude Code

↑ Back to top
Follow Claude Code’s MCP instructions for your installed client version. Add the copied endpoint with:
claude mcp add --transport http woocommerce-ai "YOUR_COPIED_SERVER_URL"
In Claude Code, open /mcp and complete the authentication flow when prompted. The WordPress.com connection uses OAuth on first use; this path does not require copying a WooCommerce consumer secret into the client configuration.

...

Optional: direct API-key connection

↑ Back to top
Developers can connect directly to the store endpoint using a WooCommerce REST API key. Use the endpoint:
your-store.example/wp-json/woocommerce-ai/mcp
The direct transport accepts the X-MCP-API-Key header in consumer_key:consumer_secret format. Use a dedicated key with the least required permission and keep its secret in the client’s supported secure configuration. Read keys permit read operations; write or read/write keys permit the corresponding writes. Keep the key out of screenshots and shared files.
Follow your client’s official instructions for adding the API-key header.

# Authentication

WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API. It is also possible to authenticate using any [WP REST API authentication](v3.wp-api.org/guide/authentication/) plugin or method.

## REST API keys

Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints. New keys can be generated either through the WordPress admin interface or they can be auto-generated through an endpoint.

### Generating API keys in the WordPress admin interface

To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API.

*Note: Keys/Apps was found at WooCommerce > Settings > API > Key/Apps prior to WooCommerce 3.4.*

[image: WooCommerce REST API keys settings]

Click the "Add Key" button. In the next screen, add a description and select the WordPress user you would like to generate the key for. Use of the REST API with the generated keys will conform to that user's WordPress roles and capabilities.

Choose the level of access for this REST API key, which can be _Read_ access, _Write_ access or _Read/Write_ access. Then click the "Generate API Key" button and WooCommerce will generate REST API keys for the selected user.

[image: Creating a new REST API key]

Now that keys have been generated, you should see two new keys, a QRCode, and a Revoke API Key button. These two keys are your Consumer Key and Consumer Secret.

[image: Generated REST API key]

If the WordPress user associated with an API key is deleted, the API key will cease to function. API keys are not transferred to other users.

### Auto generating API keys using our Application Authentication Endpoint

This endpoint can be used by any APP to *allow users to generate API keys* for your APP. This makes integration with WooCommerce API easier because the user only needs to grant access to your APP via a URL. After being redirected back to your APP, the API keys will be sent back in a separate POST request.

The following image illustrates how this works:

[image: Authentication Endpoint flow]

:::warning
This endpoint works exclusively for users to generate API keys and facilitate integration between the WooCommerce REST API and an application. In no way is this endpoint intended to be used as login method for customers.
:::

...

| `user_id`      | string | User ID in your APP. For your internal reference, used when the user is redirected back to your APP. NOT THE USER ID IN WOOCOMMERCE `MANDATORY` |
| `return_url`   | string | URL the user will be redirected to after authentication `MANDATORY`                                                                             |
| `callback_url` | string | URL that will receive the generated API key. Note: this URL should be over **HTTPS** `MANDATORY`                                                |

...

- The auth endpoint will send the API Keys in JSON format to the `callback_url`, so it's important to remember that some languages such as PHP will not display it inside the `$_POST` global variable, in PHP you can access it using `$HTTP_RAW_POST_DATA` (for old PHP versions) or `file_get_contents('php://input');`.
- The URL generated must have all query string values encoded.

## Authentication over HTTPS

You may use [HTTP Basic Auth](en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication) by providing the REST API Consumer Key as the username and the REST API Consumer Secret as the password.

> HTTP Basic Auth example

...

## Authentication over HTTP

You must use [OAuth 1.0a "one-legged" authentication](tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5849) to ensure REST API credentials cannot be intercepted by an attacker. Typically you will use any standard OAuth 1.0a library in the language of your choice to handle the authentication, or generate the necessary parameters by following the following instructions.

### Creating a signature

#### Collect the request method and URL

First you need to determine the HTTP method you will be using for the request, and the URL of the request.

The **HTTP method** will be `GET` in our case.

The **Request URL** will be the endpoint you are posting to, e.g. `example.com/wp-json/wc/v3/orders`.

#### Collect parameters

Collect and normalize your parameters. This includes all `oauth_*` parameters except for the `oauth_signature` itself.

...

#### Generate the signature

Generate the signature using the *signature base string* and your consumer secret key with a `&` character with the HMAC-SHA1 hashing algorithm.

In PHP you can use the [hash_hmac](php.net/manual/en/function.hash-hmac.php) function.

HMAC-SHA1 or HMAC-SHA256 are the only accepted hash algorithms.

If you are having trouble generating a correct signature, you'll want to review the string you are signing for encoding errors. The [authentication source](github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/master/includes/class-wc-rest-authentication.php#L185) can also be helpful in understanding how to properly generate the signature.

### OAuth tips

* The OAuth parameters may be added as query string parameters or included in the Authorization header.
* Note there is no reliable cross-platform way to get the raw request headers in WordPress, so query string should be more reliable in some cases.

excerpts:
post_title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration sidebar_label: MCP Integration category_slug: mcp

Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration

Introduction

WooCommerce registers product and order abilities in WordPress. With the MCP Adapter plugin, AI clients can discover and run these store operations through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), subject to WordPress and WooCommerce permissions.
:::info
Developer Preview Notice The MCP implementation in WooCommerce is currently in developer preview. Implementation details, APIs, and integration patterns may change in future releases as the feature matures.
:::

Enabling MCP Integration

WooCommerce always registers its abilities through the WordPress Abilities API; there is no WooCommerce setting to turn on. To make them available to MCP clients, install and activate the MCP Adapter plugin:
wp plugin install mcp-adapter --activate
WooCommerce does not bundle the MCP adapter.

Authentication and Security

WordPress Application Password Requirements

Remote HTTP connections authenticate using a WordPress username and an Application Password. Do not use your account password or a WooCommerce REST API key.
To create an Application Password:
1. In the WordPress dashboard, navigate to Users → Profile.
2. Under Application Passwords, enter a name for the MCP client.
3. Click Add New Application Password.
4. Copy the generated password and store it securely. WordPress only displays it once.
Use the WordPress username and generated password as WP_API_USERNAME and WP_API_PASSWORD in the remote proxy configuration. Application Passwords can be revoked independently from the user's profile.

HTTPS Enforcement

Use HTTPS for remote HTTP connections so credentials are encrypted in transit. Local STDIO connections authenticate through WP-CLI using the configured --user and do not require an Application Password.

Permission Validation

The MCP Adapter authenticates requests as the WordPress user associated with the Application Password. The default server requires an authenticated user with the read capability, and each WooCommerce ability also enforces its own permission callback. Use a dedicated WordPress user with only the capabilities the MCP client needs.

Server Endpoint

WooCommerce abilities are available through the WordPress MCP Adapter's default server:
yourstore.com/wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server
The WooCommerce-specific /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint was removed in WooCommerce 11.3. See Removed in WooCommerce 11.3.

...

Order Management

* Query orders with filtering and pagination
* Query notes for an order (woocommerce/order-notes-query)
* Update order status
* Add order notes
All operations respect WooCommerce's existing permission system. MCP clients authenticate through the MCP Adapter as a WordPress user.

Removed in WooCommerce 11.3

WooCommerce 11.3 removed the deprecated WooCommerce MCP endpoint and everything that only existed to support it:
* The /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint and its WooCommerce REST API key authentication (X-MCP-API-Key). Requests to the endpoint now return HTTP 410 with a JSON-RPC error that explains how to connect through the MCP Adapter.
* The REST-derived product and order abilities (woocommerce/products-list, woocommerce/orders-get, and similar), along with the woocommerce_mcp_include_ability, woocommerce_mcp_allow_insecure_transport, and woocommerce_check_rest_ability_permissions_for_method filters and the expose_in_deprecated_woocommerce_mcp ability metadata.

Getting Started with WooCommerce APIs

WooCommerce provides a number of programmatic APIs to interact with WooCommerce store data.

WC REST API

The WC REST API is a powerful part of WooCommerce which lets you read and write various parts of WooCommerce data such as orders, products, coupons, customers, and shipping zones. It based on the WordPress REST API.
Explore the WC REST API documentation.

Store API

The Store API provides public REST API endpoints for the development of customer-facing cart, checkout, and product functionality. In contrast to the WooCommerce REST API, the Store API is unauthenticated and does not provide access to sensitive store data or other customer information.
Explore the Store API documentation.

Dual API (code + GraphQL, experimental)

# WooCommerce REST API

The WooCommerce REST API connects your store to external systems and services. Most integrations require you to generate API keys in WooCommerce and enter them in the external service to establish the connection. This document covers how to generate and manage REST API keys from a merchant perspective, with links to developer documentation for more advanced topics.

**Note:** You can find the technical documentation for the REST API on GitHub.

The WooCommerce REST API uses a key system to control access. Each set of keys is linked to a WordPress user on your site. You can create keys with different permission levels depending on what the connected application needs.

To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user:

1. Go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API**.

3. Enter a **Description** to identify what the key is used for.
4. Select the **User** you want to generate a key for from the dropdown.

6. Select **Generate API Key**.

After generating the key, the screen displays your **Consumer Key**, **Consumer Secret**, a **QR Code**, and a **Revoke Key** link. Copy the **Consumer Key** and **Consumer Secret** and enter them in the application you are connecting to. The application may also request your site URL.

**Note:** The Consumer Secret is shown only once. Copy and store it in a safe place before leaving the page.



The legacy REST API has been removed from WooCommerce core. WooCommerce now integrates directly with the WordPress REST API. If an integration on your site still requires the legacy REST API, install and activate the WooCommerce Legacy REST API plugin from WordPress.org.

Webhooks configured to use the legacy REST API also stop working unless you install this plugin.

After installing and activating the plugin, go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Legacy API** and select the **Enable the legacy REST API** checkbox.

If you need to test or build custom integrations with the REST API, the following developer resources provide detailed technical guidance:

* Make a basic request — walks through requesting order data from your site to confirm the API is working.
* WooCommerce REST API Docs — the complete technical reference for all available endpoints.

sources.trimmed:
WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API. It is also possible to authenticate using any WP REST API authentication plugin or method.

## REST API keys

Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints. New keys can be generated either through the WordPress admin interface or they can be auto-generated through an endpoint.

### Generating API keys in the WordPress admin interface

To create or manage keys for a specific WordPress user, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API.

*Note: Keys/Apps was found at WooCommerce > Settings > API > Key/Apps prior to WooCommerce 3.4.*

Click the "Add Key" button. In the next screen, add a description and select the WordPress user you would like to generate the key for. Use of the REST API with the generated keys will conform to that user's WordPress roles and capabilities.

Choose the level of access for this REST API key, which can be *Read* access, *Write* access or *Read/Write* access. Then click the "Generate API Key" button and WooCommerce will generate REST API keys for the selected user.

Now that keys have been generated, you should see two new keys, a QRCode, and a Revoke API Key button. These two keys are your Consumer Key and Consumer Secret.

If the WordPress user associated with an API key is deleted, the API key will cease to function. API keys are not transferred to other users.

### Auto generating API keys using our Application Authentication Endpoint

This endpoint can be used by any APP to *allow users to generate API keys* for your APP. This makes integration with WooCommerce API easier because the user only needs to grant access to your APP via a URL. After being redirected back to your APP, the API keys will be sent back in a separate POST request.

The following image illustrates how this works:

warning

This endpoint works exclusively for users to generate API keys and facilitate integration between the WooCommerce REST API and an application. In no way is this endpoint intended to be used as login method for customers.

#### URL parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app_name` | string | Your APP name `MANDATORY` |
| `scope` | string | Level of access. Available: `read`, `write` and `read_write` `MANDATORY` |
| `user_id` | string | User ID in your APP. For your internal reference, used when the user is redirected back to your APP. NOT THE USER ID IN WOOCOMMERCE `MANDATORY` |
| `return_url` | string | URL the user will be redirected to after authentication `MANDATORY` |
| `callback_url` | string | URL that will receive the generated API key. Note: this URL should be over **HTTPS** `MANDATORY` |

#### Creating an authentication endpoint URL

You must use the `/wc-auth/v1/authorize` endpoint and pass the above parameters as a query string.

> Example of how to build an authentication URL:

* cURL
* JavaScript
* PHP
* Python
* Ruby

```
# Bash example



STORE_URL='http://example.com'



ENDPOINT='/wc-auth/v1/authorize'



PARAMS="app_name=My App Name&scope=read_write&user_id=123&return_url=http://app.com/return-page&callback_url=https://app.com/callback-endpoint"



QUERY_STRING="$(perl -MURI::Escape -e 'print uri_escape($ARGV[0]);' "$PARAMS")"



QUERY_STRING=$(echo $QUERY_STRING | sed -e "s/%20/\+/g" -e "s/%3D/\=/g" -e "s/%26/\&/g")



echo "$STORE_URL$ENDPOINT?$QUERY_STRING"
```

};



const query_string = querystring.stringify(params).replace(/%20/g, '+');



console.log(store_url + endpoint + '?' + query_string);
```

sources.trimmed:
# Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration

## Introduction

WooCommerce registers product and order abilities in WordPress. With the MCP Adapter plugin, AI clients can discover and run these store operations through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), subject to WordPress and WooCommerce permissions.

Developer Preview Notice The MCP implementation in WooCommerce is currently in developer preview. Implementation details, APIs, and integration patterns may change in future releases as the feature matures.

## Enabling MCP Integration

WooCommerce always registers its abilities through the WordPress Abilities API; there is no WooCommerce setting to turn on. To make them available to MCP clients, install and activate the MCP Adapter plugin:

```
```
wp plugin install mcp-adapter --activate
```
```

WooCommerce does not bundle the MCP adapter.

## Authentication and Security

### WordPress Application Password Requirements

Remote HTTP connections authenticate using a WordPress username and an Application Password. Do not use your account password or a WooCommerce REST API key.

To create an Application Password:

* In the WordPress dashboard, navigate to Users → Profile.
* Under Application Passwords, enter a name for the MCP client.
* Click Add New Application Password.
* Copy the generated password and store it securely. WordPress only displays it once.

Use the WordPress username and generated password as

```
WP_API_USERNAME
```

and

```
WP_API_PASSWORD
```

in the remote proxy configuration. Application Passwords can be revoked independently from the user's profile.

### HTTPS Enforcement

Use HTTPS for remote HTTP connections so credentials are encrypted in transit. Local STDIO connections authenticate through WP-CLI using the configured

```
--user
```

and do not require an Application Password.

### Permission Validation

The MCP Adapter authenticates requests as the WordPress user associated with the Application Password. The default server requires an authenticated user with the

```
read
```

capability, and each WooCommerce ability also enforces its own permission callback. Use a dedicated WordPress user with only the capabilities the MCP client needs.

## Server Endpoint

WooCommerce abilities are available through the WordPress MCP Adapter's default server:

```
```
https://yourstore.com/wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server
```
```

The WooCommerce-specific

```
/wp-json/woocommerce/mcp
```

endpoint was removed in WooCommerce 11.3. See Removed in WooCommerce 11.3.

## Connecting to the MCP Server

Choose a connection method based on where the WordPress site is running. For a detailed overview and application-specific instructions, see Connecting AI applications and the wordpress/mcp-adaptor repository.

### Local Sites Using STDIO

For a local WordPress installation, MCP clients can connect directly through the MCP Adapter's WP-CLI command. The client needs access to the WordPress files and a working WP-CLI installation.

#### JSON Configuration

Add the following server to your MCP client configuration. Replace the WordPress path and user with values from your local environment:

```
```
{  
  "mcpServers": {  
    "woocommerce_store": {  
      "command": "wp",  
      "args": [  
        "--path=/path/to/your/wordpress/site",  
        "mcp-adapter",  
        "serve",  
        "--server=mcp-adapter-default-server",  
        "--user=admin"  
      ]  
    }  
  }  
}
```
```

Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Cursor use the

```
mcpServers
```

property shown above. For VS Code, use

```
servers
```

instead.

#### Command-Line Configuration

Claude Code users can add the same server from the command line:

```
```
claude mcp add woocommerce_store -- \  
  wp --path=/path/to/your/wordpress/site \  
  mcp-adapter serve \  
  --server=mcp-adapter-default-server \  
  --user=admin
```
```

You can verify the server directly with WP-CLI:

```
```
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'

# Connect an AI client to the WooCommerce AI MCP server

Connect an external Model Context Protocol (MCP) client to your store’s WooCommerce AI server. Use the endpoint generated for your store, then authorize the client and confirm a read-only request before allowing store changes.

**Note**:

This is a **Developer level** doc. If you are unfamiliar working with code and resolving potential conflicts, we recommend you work with a Woo Agency Partner for larger projects, or find a WooCommerce developer on **Codeable** for smaller customizations. We are unable to provide support for customizations under our**Support Policy**.

* WooCommerce and WooCommerce AI are active.
* Your store and user account are connected to WordPress.com.
* Your account can manage WooCommerce.
* The MCP client supports remote HTTP servers and the authentication flow used by the endpoint.

1. In WordPress admin, go to **WooCommerce > Settings > WooCommerce AI > Advanced > MCP server**.
2. Enable **Progressive MCP server** if it is off.
3. Open **Setup**, choose your client, and copy the generated server URL or configuration.

The WordPress.com URL includes your store identifier. Its structure is:

```
https://public-api.wordpress.com/wpcom/v2/sites/{site}/woocommerce-ai-mcp/v1
```

Copy the complete URL from your store’s **Setup** screen, including its store identifier.

Follow Claude Code’s MCP instructions for your installed client version. Add the copied endpoint with:

```
claude mcp add --transport http woocommerce-ai "YOUR_COPIED_SERVER_URL"
```
